name: ServiceNow
summary: ServiceNow builds a cloud platform that companies use to run workflows in IT, HR, customer service and more. Its careers site describes three stages (application, interviews and a decision) and says some roles include a technical coding assessment or a presentation. Candidates commonly report several interviews covering technical depth, past work and how you fit its values, which include 'Wow our customers'.
rounds: Recruiter screen after an application review
Online coding assessment for many engineering roles
Technical interviews, often two or three: coding, problem solving and system design for experienced roles
A presentation for some roles, such as pre-sales and consulting
Hiring manager interview on past work and values
looks_for: Working as one team across engineering, product and sales
Drive to learn, with humility about what you don't know
Understanding of how large organisations run IT, HR and service work

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went beyond what a customer or user expected.
covers: What they expected and what they really needed
What you did beyond it and why
How they reacted, with evidence if you have it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate succeed, even though it wasn't your task.
covers: What the teammate was stuck on
What you did and how you balanced it with your own work
The result for them and for the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical. How did you find out, and what did you change?
covers: What you believed and why it seemed right
How you found out: data, a review, a failure
How you handled it openly and what you do differently now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped someone new to the team feel included.
covers: Who they were and what made joining hard
Specific things you did, beyond being friendly
How they settled in and what you learned

questions.text: What is IT service management? Explain the difference between an incident and a problem to a new joiner.
covers: Running IT as services for people, with requests, incidents and changes
An incident is one disruption to restore fast; a problem is its underlying cause
A simple example, such as repeated email outages traced to one server

questions.text: How would you design a ticketing system that routes each request to the right team automatically?
covers: What a ticket holds and how requests come in: portal, email, chat
Routing by rules first, then learning from past tickets
Fallbacks when routing is unsure, and measuring time to resolution

questions.text: How would you design approval workflows, such as a laptop request needing a manager's sign-off, so steps can change without new code?
covers: Defining workflows as data: steps, conditions, approvers
A workflow engine that runs them and records each step
Versioning changes so requests already in progress aren't broken

questions.text: A workflow that ran fine yesterday is now timing out for one large customer. How would you find the cause?
covers: What changed: data volume, a configuration, a release
Tracing the slow step with logs and timings
A safe fix for the customer and a guard so it doesn't recur

questions.text: How would you make search fast across millions of records in a web application?
covers: Indexes, or a search engine built on an inverted index
Keeping the index up to date as records change
Paging, caching and measuring slow queries

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd present our platform to a customer's head of IT whose request process is slow and manual.
covers: Starting from their pain: delays, lost requests, no visibility
Showing one workflow before and after, not every feature
The outcome they'd measure and a clear next step

questions.text: Explain REST APIs, and how you'd connect two business systems so their data stays in sync.
covers: Resources, HTTP methods and status codes in plain words
Choosing between events or webhooks and scheduled syncs
Handling failures: retries, duplicates and conflicting changes

questions.text: Why ServiceNow? What do you think its platform does for the companies that use it?
covers: A clear picture of what the platform does, in a sentence or two
A reason tied to the role or team
What you'd bring to it

questions.text: ServiceNow's purpose is to make the world work better for everyone. What would that mean in the work you'd do here?
covers: Who benefits from the work: employees, customers, IT teams
An example of a frustrating process that software could fix
How your role would contribute

questions.text: What questions do you have for us about the team or the role?
covers: Two or three questions you couldn't answer from the website
Questions about how success is measured and how the team works
Something that shows you've listened during the interview

tips: ServiceNow says interviews, tests and technical challenges must be done without AI help unless it tells you otherwise, so practise solving problems on your own.
Learn the basics of IT service management (incidents, requests, changes) so you can talk about the problems the platform solves.
For a presentation, start with the customer's problem and the outcome, then show how the solution gets there.
Prepare a story about customer impact and one about helping your team; interviewers commonly probe both.
ServiceNow University offers no-cost courses and certifications on the platform; a short course can help you talk about it with confidence.
